verdict: Xcel's net income nearly doubled to $960 million — mostly because last year's quarter carried a $287 million Marshall wildfire charge versus $1 million this year — while recovery of grid investments and warm weather lifted underlying earnings per share 23%.

kpis.note: operating revenues, +6.6% vs a year ago

kpis.note: vs $524M a year ago, when wildfire charges hit

otherDetail: Interest charges and financing costs of $432M (interest of $484M less a $52M AFUDC-debt credit), partly offset by a $131M AFUDC-equity credit and $62M of other income, net — plus $77M of equity-method earnings counted separately; a net $162M cost in total.
oneTimers: Marshall Wildfire litigation cost just $1M this quarter, versus a $287M charge in Q3 2025 — that swing is the main reason GAAP net income rose 83% year over year. Xcel's 'ongoing' EPS excludes the charge in both periods.
Earnings from equity method investments jumped to $77M from $6M a year ago, adding to the year-over-year increase.

takeaways.title: The wildfire swing
takeaways.text: Marshall wildfire litigation cost $1M this quarter versus a $287M charge a year ago — that comparison alone explains most of the jump in GAAP profit, from $524M to $960M.

takeaways.title: Underlying earnings grew
takeaways.text: Ongoing EPS — Xcel's non-GAAP measure without the wildfire charge — rose to $1.52 from $1.24, on recovery of electric infrastructure investment and unseasonably warm weather, partly offset by higher financing costs.

takeaways.title: 2027 guidance initiated
takeaways.text: Xcel narrowed 2026 ongoing EPS guidance to $4.10–$4.16 and guided 2027 at $4.48–$4.62, targeting 6–8%+ annual EPS growth as it builds clean generation and transmission.

footerNote: Utility layout: energy supply costs — electric fuel and purchased power of $1,067M, cost of natural gas sold and transported of $58M and $2M of other cost of sales — are the direct-cost block. Net income is the consolidated $960M, which is also the GAAP earnings figure attributable to common shareholders ($1.52 per diluted share) in Xcel's release. AFUDC is the allowance for funds used during construction — a regulated-utility credit for money tied up in projects being built.
